title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2606.03043v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM judges now score most open-ended NLP output, and their mutual agreement is routinely read as evidence that the scores can be trusted. That reading is unsafe: judges may agree because they capture quality, or because they share the same blind spots, and agreement statistics alone cannot tell these apart. We develop a geometric test that can. Treating each judge's scores as a vector, we measure spread, effective rank, the angle to human scores, and the judge-judge, judge-human, and human-human agreement triple for 42 judges on two community-built Indic benchmarks covering four domains and eight languages. Every comparison is reference-matched: a judge and a held-out rater are scored against the same two-rater mean, since an averaged reference otherwise flatters judges by several degrees. On subjective rubrics, judges agree with one another as much as humans do yet reach only 58-66% of human agreement and often concentrate on an axi

translated_title: LLM作为评判者的几何学：为什么LLM之间的共识并不等于人类对齐
translated_abstract: 如今，大语言模型（LLM）评判者对大多数开放式NLP输出进行打分，它们之间的一致性通常被视为分数可信的证据。但这种解读并不安全：评判者之间达成一致，可能是因为它们真正捕捉到了质量，也可能是因为它们共享同样的盲点，而仅凭一致性统计无法区分这两种情况。我们开发了一种能够进行这种区分的几何测试。我们将每个评判者的分数视为一个向量，在两个由社区构建、覆盖四个领域和八种语言的印度语系基准上，对42个评判者测量其分数的离散度、有效秩、与人类分数的夹角，以及评判者-评判者、评判者-人类、人类-人类一致性三元组。每一项比较都是参考匹配的：评判者与一个留出评分者都针对相同的双人评分均值进行评分，因为若非如此，平均参考值会以数度之差美化评判者的表现。在主观评分标准上，评判者之间的一致程度与人类相当，但仅达到人类一致性的58-66%，并且常常集中于某个轴上……
tldr: 本文提出一种将LLM评判者分数视为向量并通过测量离散度、有效秩、与人类分数夹角及一致性三元组的几何检验方法，揭示了LLM之间的相互共识不能等同于与人类判断的对齐——评判者在主观标准上彼此一致程度接近人类，但与人类评分的一致性仅达58-66%，原因在于它们可能共享同样的盲点。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a geometric test that treats each LLM judge's scores as a vector and measures spread, effective rank, angles to human scores, and agreement triples, showing that inter-LLM consensus does not imply human alignment, since judges agree with each other as much as humans do yet reach only 58-66% of human agreement, likely due to shared blind spots.
